heroIntro: A burst pipe puts water into your structure faster than almost any other failure mode. Every minute between rupture and shutoff adds volume to the loss — and every hour between shutoff and extraction determines how far that water penetrates walls, flooring, and subfloor. whatItIs.heading: What is pipe burst flooding and remediation?
whatItIs.body: Pipe burst flooding is water damage caused by the sudden failure of a supply line, distribution pipe, or hose bib — releasing pressurized water into the structure. In Southern California, common failure patterns include aging galvanized steel pipes in Sun City and older Inland Empire tracts corroding from the inside out, copper supply lines in 1980s and 1990s tract homes developing pinhole leaks that progress to full failure, PEX hose bib connections at exterior walls failing during rare freeze events, and washer supply lines and toilet supply tubes rupturing at the valve. Unlike a slow leak, a burst pipe delivers water at line pressure until it's shut off — a supply line running unchecked for 30 minutes can deposit hundreds of gallons into a structure. Remediation is the full response: shutoff coordination, extraction, structural drying, mold prevention, and reconstruction.

process.heading: How we handle pipe burst flooding and remediation

steps.title: Shutoff confirmation and emergency extraction
steps.body: We verify the water source is isolated — coordinating with your plumber or guiding you to the main shutoff — before extraction begins. No extraction equipment goes into an active flow. Once isolated, high-volume extraction begins immediately to remove standing water from all affected surfaces.

steps.title: Moisture mapping and controlled demolition
steps.body: Pressurized water from a burst pipe travels far beyond the visible wet area. We use thermal imaging and moisture meters to map the full extent of saturation, then remove wet drywall, flooring, and insulation to the extent necessary to expose the structural cavity for drying. We don't guess where to stop — we follow the moisture readings.

steps.title: Structural drying, remediation, and rebuild
steps.body: Commercial air movers and dehumidifiers run until all structural readings reach dry standard — typically 3 to 7 days. Antimicrobial treatment is applied where indicated. Once dry, Gallagher Restoration handles drywall, flooring, and finish restoration, and coordinates with your plumber on the pipe repair sequencing so demolition access and reconstruction don't conflict.

signs.heading: Signs you're dealing with pipe burst flooding now
signs.intro: Pipe burst events are usually obvious — but the full extent of damage often isn't. These are the indicators that require immediate professional response.

items.title: Sudden, unexplained drop in water pressure
items.body: A significant pressure drop throughout the house — not just at one fixture — often means a main or distribution line has failed. Locate your main shutoff and call immediately.

items.title: Sound of running water with all fixtures off
items.body: If you can hear water movement inside walls or under floors with everything turned off, a pipe is actively discharging into the structure. This is a shutoff-and-call emergency.

items.title: Visible flooding on any floor level
items.body: Standing water on any floor surface from a supply-line event is a pipe burst scenario until proven otherwise. The volume present is only part of what was released — most of it is already in the subfloor.

items.title: Wet or warping flooring without a visible source
items.body: Hardwood cupping, laminate swelling, or soft spots in tile grout lines can indicate a slab leak or under-slab pipe failure. These events discharge water slowly enough that visible flooding may never occur.

items.title: Water staining on lower walls after a freeze event
items.body: Southern California's freeze events are infrequent but occur in inland and higher-elevation areas of Riverside and San Bernardino counties. A pipe that froze and thawed may not show failure until water pressure is restored. Inspect supply lines in exterior walls and unconditioned spaces after any hard freeze.

whyUs.heading: Full incident management, not just cleanup.
whyUs.body: Pipe burst flooding is the highest-urgency water event most homeowners will face. The cost of the loss is almost entirely determined by two variables: how fast the water was shut off and how fast extraction began. Everything that happens after shutoff — extraction depth, moisture mapping accuracy, drying duration, reconstruction quality — determines whether your home comes back in three weeks or three months. Gallagher Restoration Co. has managed pipe burst events across Riverside, San Bernardino, Orange, San Diego, and Los Angeles counties for over 15 years. Aaron built the company's response model around the understanding that these calls come at 2 a.m., during holidays, and during the same storm that's affecting your neighbor's house. A real person answers every call. We're typically on-site within 60 minutes. Our IICRC-trained technicians handle extraction through reconstruction under one agreement, coordinating directly with your plumber and your insurance adjuster so you have one point of contact — not four.

pricing.heading: Pipe burst flooding and remediation costs
pricing.body: Pipe burst flooding and remediation in Southern California typically runs $2,000 to $18,000. The range is wide because the primary cost driver is time — specifically, how long water ran before shutoff and how long it sat before extraction. A washer supply line caught in under 10 minutes with immediate extraction sits at the lower end. A main line running overnight in an unoccupied home, saturating multiple rooms and the subfloor throughout, sits at the upper end. Other variables include affected floor area, whether hardwood or other non-restorable flooring must be replaced, extent of drywall demolition required to expose and dry the cavity, and whether mold remediation is needed. Gallagher Restoration provides a free on-site assessment. Pipe burst events from supply line failures are covered under most homeowner's policies. We document scope and coordinate directly with your insurance carrier.

faqs.q: What's the first thing I should do when a pipe bursts?
faqs.a: Shut off the water at the main supply valve immediately — this is the single most important action you can take. Every minute of active flow adds to the damage scope. Main shutoffs are typically at the meter near the street or at the pressure regulator near where the line enters the home. Once the water is off, call Gallagher Restoration at (951) 541-0034. Don't start mopping or moving belongings until we've assessed the situation — disturbing the water can spread contamination and complicate insurance documentation.

faqs.q: Do I need a plumber and a restoration company, or can one handle everything?
faqs.a: You need both for separate scopes. A plumber repairs or replaces the failed pipe. A restoration company extracts the water, dries the structure, remediates any mold, and repairs the damaged drywall, flooring, and finishes. Gallagher Restoration coordinates directly with your plumber to sequence access and reconstruction so the two scopes don't conflict.

faqs.q: How long does remediation take after a pipe burst?
faqs.a: Structural drying typically takes 3 to 7 days after extraction is complete. Reconstruction — drywall, flooring, paint — follows drying and typically adds 1 to 3 weeks depending on scope. Total project duration from emergency response to finished restoration runs 2 to 5 weeks for most residential pipe burst events. Larger losses with multi-room impact or subfloor replacement take longer.

faqs.q: Is pipe burst flooding covered by homeowner's insurance?
faqs.a: Sudden and accidental pipe failures are covered under most standard homeowner's policies as a named peril. Gradual leaks — a slow drip that caused damage over months — are typically excluded as maintenance failures. Slab leaks exist in a gray area: the pipe repair itself is usually not covered, but the resulting water damage often is. Gallagher Restoration documents the full loss from arrival and works directly with your adjuster to establish the covered scope.
